question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $17,$ the additive inverse of $-56$ modulo $17$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $-56$ modulo $17$ is the integer $0\le x<17$ such that

$$
x+(-56)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,17).
$$

First, we note that $-56≡12\,(\text{mod}\,17):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}-56 & ≡(-4)\cdot 17+12 & \,(\text{mod}\,17) \\  & ≡(-4)\cdot 0+12 & \,(\text{mod}\,17) \\  & ≡12 & \,(\text{mod}\,17)\end{aligned}
$$

Also, note that $-12+12≡0,$ so $x≡-12\,(\text{mod}\,17).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-12 & \,(\text{mod}\,17) \\  & ≡0-12 & \,(\text{mod}\,17) \\  & ≡17-12 & \,(\text{mod}\,17) \\  & ≡5 & \,(\text{mod}\,17)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $-56$ modulo $17$ is $5.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-56+5≡-51≡(-3)\cdot 17≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,17)\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
